categories.main_business_segments: Miyaji Engineering Group operates primarily through two business segments: Miyaji Engineering, which focuses on the design, fabrication, and construction of new steel bridges, maintenance and reinforcement of existing bridges, and large-scale/high-rise buildings; and MM Bridge, which specializes in the design, manufacture, installation, and repair of bridges and coastal structures. Both segments are deeply involved in social infrastructure projects, including civil engineering and steel structure works.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced steel structure engineering, including high-efficiency welding, robotic automation, and digital transformation (DX) in manufacturing. It is also engaged in the development of FRP (fiber-reinforced plastic) structures, composite steel-concrete technologies, and innovative monitoring systems for infrastructure health. The group emphasizes productivity improvements through automation, digital tools (BIM/CIM, drones, AI), and environmentally friendly construction methods.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers are public sector entities such as the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism, expressway companies (e.g., West Nippon Expressway), and local governments, as well as major private sector clients like railway companies and large general contractors. The group’s main markets are public infrastructure projects, including bridges, highways, and railway-related construction, with a growing focus on maintenance and renewal of aging infrastructure.
categories.geographic_coverage: Operations are concentrated in Japan, with headquarters in Tokyo and major production facilities in Chiba and other regions. The company has a nationwide presence through multiple offices and project sites, but over 90% of sales are domestic, with no significant overseas assets or sales reported.
categories.supply_chain_position: Miyaji Engineering Group operates as a midstream and downstream player in the construction and engineering supply chain, providing design, fabrication, and installation services for steel structures and infrastructure projects. It procures raw materials (mainly steel) from upstream suppliers and delivers finished infrastructure to public and private sector clients.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include strengthening the management structure, enhancing productivity through DX and automation, and expanding into maintenance and renewal markets. R&D focuses on cost reduction, quality improvement, new materials (e.g., FRP), environmental technologies, and digital solutions for infrastructure monitoring and construction efficiency. The company is also committed to sustainability, carbon neutrality, and diversity in human resources.
categories.revenue_model: The group generates revenue primarily through contract-based sales for construction projects, including design, fabrication, and installation of steel structures. Revenue is recognized based on project progress (percentage-of-completion method), with additional income from maintenance services and, to a lesser extent, sales of proprietary products and technologies.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include other large Japanese steel structure and bridge engineering firms such as Komaihaltec, Yokogawa Bridge, and Hitachi Zosen. Miyaji Engineering Group is positioned as a leading player in the domestic steel bridge and infrastructure market, with a reputation for technical excellence and the ability to handle large-scale, complex projects.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated net sales reached 74.7 billion yen, with operating profit of 9.2 billion yen and net income attributable to parent company shareholders of 4.9 billion yen. The company has shown steady growth in sales and profits over the past several years, achieving record-high results in FY2024 and FY2025, and targets further growth with a mid-term plan aiming for 68 billion yen in sales by FY2026.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Miyaji Engineering Group differentiates itself through advanced engineering capabilities, a strong track record in large and technically demanding infrastructure projects, and a commitment to safety, quality, and sustainability. The company emphasizes its ability to deliver high-value, reliable solutions for both new construction and the renewal of aging infrastructure, leveraging digital innovation and environmental technologies to meet evolving societal needs.
